claim: Let \(K\) be the standard six-vertex triangulation of \(\mathbb{RP}^2\). Exactly \(428{,}400\) acyclic Hasse matchings on \(K\) have discrete Morse vector \((1,1,1)\), equivalently exactly \(428{,}400\) discrete gradient vector fields are \(\mathbf F_2\)-perfect. Forgetting the critical vertex and critical triangle gives \(7{,}140\) tree-cotree decompositions; across the \(1{,}296\) primal spanning trees, the complementary dual unicycle has cycle length \(5\), \(6\), or \(9\) in exactly \(726\), \(540\), or \(30\) cases, and each of the \(15\) edges is critical in exactly \(28{,}560\) perfect fields.
integrity: The exact finite census is reproduced by an embedded standard-library verifier; literature comparison distinguishes existence and general tree-cotree theory from the new exact counts.
scientific_limitations: Exact enumeration is for the standard six-vertex triangulation only.
Perfectness is with coefficients in \(\mathbf F_2\).
No count of real-valued functions inducing the same gradient field is claimed.
title: Exact \(\mathbf F_2\)-perfect Morse census on the six-vertex projective plane
